financials.source: Form 990 FY2024 via ProPublica Nonprofit Explorer (EIN 41-0729979, filed 2025-11-17). Total revenue $998,718,346; total expenses $1,025,460,021; net deficit -$26,741,675. communityBenefit.source: Form 990 Schedule H filed for FY2024 (EIN 41-0729979) but specific community benefit dollar amounts not extracted in available aggregator data. North Memorial reports providing charity care, health screenings, crisis intervention, pastoral care, wellness classes, transportation services, and donated facility space. taxAdvantage.notes: North Memorial Health operates two hospitals and clinics as a tax-exempt 501(c)(3) nonprofit in Minnesota and western Wisconsin. Property tax exemptions primarily in Hennepin County (Robbinsdale and Maple Grove campuses). Federal and state income tax exemptions, tax-exempt bond interest subsidies on revenue bonds issued through conduit authorities, and 340B program benefits all require quantification from financial statements and county assessor records.

layoffs.source: Star Tribune, Becker's Hospital Review, KARE 11, TCB Magazine (March 2024). North Memorial eliminated 103 jobs and closed outpatient mental health services at flagship Robbinsdale hospital, affecting approximately 3,400 mental health patients. Also downgraded neonatal care from Level 2 special care nursery to Level 1 well newborn nursery. CEO cited rising government-sponsored plan enrollment (lower reimbursement) and Hennepin County's elimination of $22M annual subsidy. Minnesota Nurses Association condemned closures as prioritizing profit over patient care. System reported $8.5M operating loss in FY2023.

S&P and Fitch do not rate North Memorial Health. Becker's Hospital Review, Minnesota House and Senate committee presentations.

program340B.source: Minnesota Department of Health report (covered by Star Tribune, circa 2024): North Memorial collected $88M via the 340B drug discount program. North Memorial operates three outpatient pharmacies (Robbinsdale campus, Maple Grove campus, Robbinsdale Specialty Center). Statewide, Minnesota hospitals and clinics paid $120M to contract pharmacies and third-party administrators; North Memorial's share not broken out. Contract pharmacy count and out-of-state percentage require HRSA OPAIS database verification. DSH status requires Schedule H verification.

acquisitions.description: North Memorial acquired Fairview Health Services' 25% stake in Maple Grove Hospital Corporation, achieving 100% ownership effective May 2022. North Memorial had held 75% since the hospital's opening. Maple Grove Hospital is Minnesota's largest birth center.
acquisitions.source: North Memorial Health press release; Fairview Health Services continuing disclosure (EMMA); Moody's March 2022 action noting guarantee rising to 100%

acquisitions.description: Sanford Health (Sioux Falls, SD; 58-hospital system) signed definitive agreement in May 2026 to acquire North Memorial Health. Closed September 1, 2026 under 10-year Minnesota Attorney General oversight agreement. Sanford committed $600M investment: $500M for Maple Grove Hospital expansion, $100M for Robbinsdale Hospital equipment and deferred maintenance, plus $15M for independent healthcare providers. North Memorial became anchor of Sanford's Twin Cities region led by CEO Trevor Sawallish with local board oversight.
acquisitions.source: Minnesota AG announcement August 28, 2026; Fox 9; Becker's Hospital Review; Healthcare Finance News; Fierce Healthcare; Minnesota Reformer; KEYC; Dakota News Now

ratios.investmentsToOperatingIncomeInterpretati: North Memorial holds a $312M investment portfolio (Dec 2024 EMMA) against persistent operating losses ($8.5M loss in FY2023; $26.7M net deficit on FY2024 Form 990). The ratio cannot be computed against a loss, but the contrast is stark: the system's accumulated financial wealth of $312M in securities — with $104M in unrealized gains — dwarfs any operating surplus the system has produced in recent years. The portfolio represents 31% of the system's $999M in total revenue.

accusation: North Memorial Health, a tax-exempt health system with $713 million in total assets, holds a $312 million investment portfolio — including $104 million in unrealized gains — while reporting consecutive operating losses and a $27 million net deficit on $999 million in revenue (FY2024 Form 990). The system collected $88 million through the 340B drug discount program while its flagship Robbinsdale hospital was losing $124 million annually, prompting its CEO to tell the Maple Grove City Council the system had reached its 'fiscal breaking point.' In FY2024, departing CEO J. Kevin Croston collected $1.77 million in compensation for approximately two months of service before handing control to Trevor Sawallish, who received $1.41 million for the remainder of the year — combined CEO pay of $3.18 million in a year the system cut 103 jobs and closed outpatient mental health services affecting 3,400 patients at its Robbinsdale hospital. Moody's has downgraded North Memorial three times in two decades — from A3 to Baa1 to Baa2 — now two notches above junk, with a March 2026 Minnesota Senate presentation warning the rating was 'in jeopardy of declining again.' Rather than stabilize independently, North Memorial sold itself to South Dakota-based Sanford Health in September 2026, requiring a 10-year Attorney General oversight agreement to protect the Level 1 trauma center, charity care, reproductive healthcare, and emergency transport services that critics feared would be cut. The system partners with the Minnesota Vikings as an official healthcare sponsor while its own nurses issued a vote of no confidence in hospital leadership.
